task.question: Derive a positive simple-anchor/pair cross-energy and covered-depth bound from the signed defect, and test the missing coverage by genuine finite exponential hole phases and their short moments.
task.domain: Finite conjugation-invariant box exponential multisets; selected separated real anchors and reflection pairs; continuous nested box operators.
assumptions: Finite distinct locations with multiplicities aggregated; pair members have equal integer multiplicities.
Selected anchors are 1/2-separated; selected pair centers are q-separated, have depths <=A0 and multiplicities <=M. These conditions need not hold for unselected pairs.
The hole family and short-limit theorem use exactly the locations and a=log(2) in README Sections 5-6.

methods: Exact finite integer multiplicity inequalities and Fraction short-limit budget difference.
Weighted g/h correlations compared with the positive complex sinc modulus; selected synthesis and slack bounds in finite exponential families.
O(k) high-precision phase sums versus small direct double sums and a separate pair-block integral.
limitations: All analytic claims are solver proof candidates; no independent-verifier receipt or formal build.
Pair-center separation or bounded local occupancy is an explicit hypothesis, not extracted from the signed defect.
The covered-pair bound leaves the hole mass H_R explicit; the genuine example refutes automatic H_R=o(N) from the one-scale hypotheses.
The hole example is a genuine finite exponential multiset, not actual zeta zeros. Its long budget holds only asymptotically and it violates the fixed shorter-scale budget.
No general decomposition into homogeneous hole phases, actual arithmetic D=o(N), weighted-to-unweighted/profile transfer, or completed two-scale error budget.
Multiplicity deletion cost does not imply small discarded Hilbert-Schmidt operator energy.
No unconditional zeta-zero proportion, RH proof/refutation, or literature-wide novelty claim.
No full repository CI, bundled inventory/record runner or upstream Lean build; only package-local structure/hash checks and bounded computation.
Gauss-Legendre and mpmath quadrature are not interval certificates; numerical tests do not prove all-size statements.
